abstract: As autonomous vehicle technology advances, understanding public acceptance of robotaxis is critical. This study investigates how media attention is associated with public acceptance through cognitive and affective risk perception and perceived social approval, and whether these associations vary by use frequency. Based on a representative survey in Wuhan, China (N = 1,163), the study specifies an integrated framework drawing on the social amplification/attenuation of risk framework and the social-inference logic of the influence of presumed influence perspective. Results show significant indirect associations between media attention and acceptance through affective risk perception and perceived social approval, while robotaxi use frequency weakens the direct media effect but does not moderate the indirect pathways. These findings offer insights into media-related psychological pathways associated with technology perceptions and acceptance among both users and non-users.

title: Media attention and public acceptance of robotaxis: A moderated mediation of risk perception and perceived social approval in embodied AI
